context_documents.title: 2026-9496 · A fixed-angle launcher deliberately shifts complexity elsewhere
context_documents.body:
# 2026-9496: A fixed-angle launcher deliberately shifts complexity elsewhere

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The interview describes a passively deploying intake/hopper, roller floor explicitly inspired by 2017 team 254, a separate feed stage, a four-X60 launcher and added brass flywheel inertia. The hood is fixed; distance changes use speed and chassis aim. Intake motion agitates the stored fuel, and the aiming system has a manual fallback.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly credits the historical floor reference and identifies the fallback as a way to keep playing when automatic aim fails. No team-stated numerical optimum for fixed hood angle is established in this passage.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Removing hood actuation reduces moving hardware, but does not remove aiming requirements. The usable trajectory envelope is now constrained by wheel speed, launch angle, release height, accuracy and the routes from which the chassis can point at the target. The passive deployment also makes initial orientation and autonomous motion part of the mechanism’s operation. A simple subsystem can therefore demand careful whole-match planning without being a poor design.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Map accuracy versus range and bus voltage, test deployment from plausible starting poses, and practice the manual-aim fallback. Do not interpret the caption’s repeated “8-inch tube” wording as a verified drum diameter.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: LYNK 9496 2026 build log
source_reviews.review_basis: Read early build posts and team answers via the public post stream.
source_reviews.facts: Documents over-hopper shot orientation, shared four-motor shaft, floor geometry, center divider removal and fixed hood with range-dependent RPM.
source_reviews.limitations: Early build figures are snapshots. The initial flywheel weights and ratios are not a final event specification.

source_reviews.title: Matterhorn controls and final release Q&A
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the team descriptions of readiness, localization, passive deployment and in-season service issues.
source_reviews.facts: Fuel can obscure the front camera, so a side camera helps. Team combines pose-based aiming, calibrated RPM and readiness checks. It selected passive intake due to complexity, mass and space.
source_reviews.limitations: The older code link in post 144 did not return the raw file. The written sequence supplies the evidence for control behavior.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Matterhorn is a fixed-hood, chassis-aimed drum with passive intake deploy and a sliding hopper. LYNK credits 254's Misfire as the archetype. Its over-hopper shot direction was chosen to fit a fast neutral-zone cycle with minimal rotation on the trench route. The architecture moves complexity into path planning, heading control, and reliable transitions from collection to launch. The team explicitly considered an active intake too costly in mass, space and tuning time.
source_review.piece_flow: Two intake rollers powered by two X44s move fuel into storage. A shallow inclined roller floor advances the pile to a separately driven indexer and into the fixed-hood drum. LYNK removed the floor divider and the corresponding shooter middle plate, creating an uninterrupted two-wide path. The driver-facing shooting action pulses the intake rollers to agitate fuel, then enables floor and indexer when heading and drum speed are ready.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The trench is tight enough that the team traversed along its long axis and turned after leaving the run. A swerve module protrudes into the fuel path, with protected CANcoder wiring. A hopper full of fuel can block the front camera, making camera placement an interface with storage rather than a standalone controls choice. The passive collector can stay exposed when a powered retract would help.

subsystems.name: Passive intake and hopper
subsystems.construction: Two powered intake rollers, passively deployed collector, sliding hopper and retention net. The team reports using roller pulses while shooting.
subsystems.operation: Intake collects fuel and its roller direction can alternate for agitation. Hopper retention and exposure depend on deployed geometry.
subsystems.team_rationale: LYNK prioritized fewer active degrees of freedom while operating near its mass limit.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Verify deployment from low traction and varying battery state. Measure whether pulsing recovers low-fill feed or interrupts entry pickup.
subsystems.interfaces: Rollers to hopper opening, deployment travel to stowed geometry, and collector extent to path and contact exposure.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: The team noted poor agitation and situations where it wanted to fold the intake. Check end stops, net tears and slide contamination.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact passive deployment sequence and slide construction, reset method and mass budget.

subsystems.name: Roller floor and uptake
subsystems.construction: Early build specified 7/8-inch tubes with 1/16-inch silicone, roughly 2.125-inch centers and ten-degree inclination. Two motors were tried on the floor after single-motor issues. Printed side guides narrow the path 0.85 inch per side.
subsystems.operation: Floor and indexer move fuel into the drum. The guides keep fuel away from pulleys. Team reported faster feed improved range spread.
subsystems.team_rationale: Removing the divider increased observed BPS. Team judged the wider path acceptable for accuracy in its tests.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Electrical limits, loaded ratio and traction can masquerade as mechanical jams. Compare time to deliver at low and full fill using current and speed traces.
subsystems.interfaces: Floor to indexer compression, indexer to drum and side guides to pulleys.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Early testing exposed low-voltage and current-limit sensitivity. Team used tape to enlarge a slightly loose idler and reported cracking at the CANcoder cover.
subsystems.unknowns: Final installed ratio, loaded current, definitive idler arrangement and late-season lane distribution.

subsystems.name: Fixed drum and shot control
subsystems.construction: Four motors on one shaft, supplemental brass and steel flywheel masses in the early build, fixed hood, and PhotonVision on Orange Pi 5 with Arducam OV2311. Side camera supplements the front.
subsystems.operation: Pose estimate selects field-relative heading. Distance lookup with interpolation sets RPM. The team describes continuous corrections and a readiness gate before feed.
subsystems.team_rationale: Simplicity left tuning time for drum PIDF, heading control and calibrated distance. The driver can still aim from pose when a fresh hub view is briefly unavailable.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A one-variable range map works only across its tested launch envelope. Pose drift, RPM recovery, or lane interaction can produce systematic misses.
subsystems.interfaces: Drivetrain yaw to shot line, floor enable to readiness, and front camera field of view to hopper load.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Log loaded RPM droop, alignment errors and vision loss before changing calibration. The bumper kit also needed an internal latch after impact dismounts.
subsystems.unknowns: Final hood angle, inertia, deployed code and shot envelope by distance.

revisions: Early tests added floor drive authority, removed the center dividers and adjusted side guides. The team later supplemented the obstructed front camera and reported the trade-offs of keeping the intake passive.
transferable_principles: Pair fixed shooter geometry with the most valuable routes. Validate the floor-to-drum handoff and readiness under full load before adding adjustability.
disconfirming_conditions: The case weakens when defense repeatedly denies the required heading, when passing needs precise bounce control, or when passive deployment fails in the available run-up.
remaining_gaps: Exact final inertia, deploy/reset geometry, drive module variant, endgame hardware and matched event measurements remain open.
